labels.notes: Cited unmarked (`defi:causal_Ealpha` — `ETT.tex:1335`, docstring l.7–8, char 197). tools/ledger.py's docstring_label_re finds no ``**`label`**`` anywhere in the file: the bold-backquoted `**`massive_line`**` has no label prefix, and in `**`ETT.tex:1341` read in `M`**` the closing backquote is not followed by `**`. The row stays partial, as it must (OQ-82, OQ-18, OQ-34/OQ-35). The l.1341 readings at M were checked by #check under `import Causal`. sing_locallyChronal takes only [TopologicalSpace M], [SingularGXStructure (Flat.isom 2) (Minkowski 2) M], [Fact (0 < κ)], hC : IsoChartsCoverDEC25 … massAModelCausality, κ ≠ 2π (harmless, since sing_{2π}(M) = ∅) and p ∈ sing M κ. It has no T2 and no absolute minimality. Its conclusion: for every open W ∋ p there are γ, t₀ and ε > 0 with γ t₀ = p, C.ChronalCurveOn W γ (t₀−ε) (t₀+ε), γ(Icc) ⊆ sing M κ, and C.lt W ordering the points. This mirrors the model's singLine_locallyChronal. « Locally chronal » is not defined in the paper (grep: only l.1341, 1345, 1531), so this is a reading, and the theorem does not say that sing_κ(M) ∩ U is the curve's image. component_timelike, at T2 M: two points of a component are equal or ≪_⊤-related, from massive_line. Both are fine readings, but the M-level reading is not new. The row already carries EModelsBPrime.causal_Ealpha_lt_singLine, an audited M-level form for the natural causality in a given chart, and the paper finding « ETT.tex:1341 … confirmed at every E_{>=0}-manifold ». sing_locallyChronal is a variant of it: any C with one isomorphic chart at each point, the chart found intrinsically, plus the chronal-curve and in-sing clauses. The REPORT's question and finding 1 do not mention it (finding 1 below). chronalCurveOn_lineσ (an inverse chart read along the line is chronal over every segment of lineJ) is the l.1531 use of this definition inside lem:past_BTZ (a), and is checked under that label.

labels.label: lem:past_BTZ
labels.notes: Not dispatched, but the file's main theorem is its (a) for α > 0. Cited unmarked (`lem:past_BTZ` — `ETT.tex:1515`, char 289), not marked anywhere. massive_line is exactly the field Causality.SingularFlatAxioms.massive_line (Causal/SingularFlat.lean:203–206) with sing := SFALocal.sing M. A probe under `import Causal` elaborated `h.massive_line = SFAMassiveLine.massive_line hC := rfl` for any h : C.SingularFlatAxioms (sing M), so the two types are definitionally equal. #check gives the hypotheses as [TopologicalSpace M], [SingularGXStructure (Flat.isom 2) (Minkowski 2) M], {C}, [T2Space M] and hC : IsoChartsCoverDEC25 (Flat.isom 2) C (minkowski 2) massAModelCausality, nothing else, as the dispatch requires. Against the paper (l.1516–1519): « M a singular spacetime » is read through DEC-25 with any causality having an isomorphic chart at each point (OQ-18). That is weaker than the paper's natural causality, which massive_line_of_isAtlasCausalityDEC25 covers with MassACovered M (the definition of an E≥0-manifold). Connectedness, second countability and absolute minimality are not used. Hausdorff is carried (DEC-25 « manifold »; ETT.tex:255). « Each connected component of sing_α(M) is an inextensible causal curve, moreover chronal » becomes the existence of γ : ℝ → M with range = the component, Inextensible ⊤ univ, ChronalCurveOn ⊤ over every segment (DEC-6), and a closed embedding when C is causal. Chronal implies causal (ChronalCurveOn.causalCurveOn). So Lean ≥ paper in the readings, for every α > 0. α = 2π is vacuous (sing_two_pi), and every α > 0 is an angle of the family. isTranslationAtlas: the index type is IsoChart C κ, the X_A-charts e : M ⇀ E_κ with IsAEChart and ChartIso C (massive κ) e. τ e = (e ·).1, σ e r = e.symm (r, apex), J e = {r | (r, apex) ∈ e.target}, V e = e.source. The cover comes from exists_isoChart: the regular branch of hC is absurd at a singular point, and the E₀ branch is excluded by mem_sing_iff_of_mem_source, i.e. cross-type invariance. trans is one prop_isom_local on e.symm.trans e′, and the clause y ∈ S is unused (filter_upwards … with y hy _). Everything is as the REPORT says. The assemblies were checked by #check. singularFlatAxioms_iff_line ([T2Space], [SecondCountableTopology], hmin, hC) is SFABTZ.singularFlatAxioms_iff_lines with massive_line discharged. hmin is needed, since absolutelyMinimal is a field of the structure; it is disclosed in the REPORT but not in the docstring (finding 3). singularFlatAxioms_of_sing_zero (h0 : sing M 0 = ∅) and singularFlatAxioms_of_massive (hpos: every singular point is in an X_A-chart into some E_κ, o ≠ none, the definition of an E_{>0}-manifold) are genuine full instances of the strict structure, built through SFALocal.singularFlatAxioms_iff, every field discharged. The only hypotheses are T2, second countability and absolute minimality (all three fields of the structure) and hC. Nothing is hidden. Witnesses: epi_singularFlatAxioms, (massive π).SingularFlatAxioms (sing (Massive π)), comes from SFALocal.nonvacuous_epi (hmin, hC, sing_0 = ∅) through singularFlatAxioms_of_sing_zero. nonvacuous_epi gives sing_π(E_π) = singLine π and a closed embedding γ onto the whole line through (0, apex). epi_hpos uses the identity chart. The claim « first SingularFlatAxioms witness with a non-empty massive line » is true. I enumerated every strict declaration that concludes SingularFlatAxioms: timelikeLine_singularFlatAxioms (fun _ => ∅); Flat/CBG flat_singularFlatAxioms and flatModelOf.singularFlatAxioms (chartedSing (fun _ => ∅)); FlatTimeCylinder (∅); E0.singularFlatAxioms_of_pushUp / singularFlatAxioms (singE0, empty for α ≠ 0); SFALocalE0 and SFALocal e0_singularFlatAxioms. All of them have sing_α = ∅ for α > 0, and so does the scaffold sibling SFALine (E₀ witnesses only). The CBG.Geometry `singularFlatAxioms` fields are hypotheses of a structure, not witnesses.

The defi:causal_Ealpha row already has an M-level anchor, EModelsBPrime.causal_Ealpha_lt_singLine (natural causality, any X_A-chart into E_κ sending x to the line, points ≪_W-ordered in every open W ∋ x). It also has a paper finding: « ETT.tex:1341 'For alpha>0 the singular line is timelike, hence locally chronal': confirmed at every E_{>=0}-manifold ». sing_locallyChronal is a variant of that anchor, under a weaker causality hypothesis and with the chart found intrinsically. findings.where: campaign/T-ett-sfa-massive-line/REPORT.json labels[0].findings[1], « "Parametrisable by R" is a homeomorphism onto the component only when M is causal »
findings.what: As worded this is too strong. Read literally, « only when » says that a non-causal M never has an embedded singular line, which is false: causality can fail away from the singular line. What holds is that the parametrisation is a closed embedding when M is causal (massive_line), and that a compact component, which forces M to be non-causal, is the image of a periodic γ. Besides, this whole point, with the by-hand example « E_κ modulo a translation along the singular line », is already the row's paper finding PF0 on l.1529–1530 (T-ett-line-development) and its findings_triage entry.
findings.fix: Do not forward it as a new finding. If anything is appended to PF0, write « (α > 0: a closed embedding when M is causal, Causal.SFAMassiveLine.massive_line) ».

findings.what: The docstring says that SingularFlatAxioms at a Hausdorff, second countable E≥0-manifold holds iff the field line does, and that absolute minimality is « not used ». singularFlatAxioms_iff_line, singularFlatAxioms_of_sing_zero and singularFlatAxioms_of_massive all take hmin : C.AbsolutelyMinimal, and they need it, because absolutelyMinimal is a field of the structure. The REPORT discloses this; the docstring does not. Row 4 (second countability) has the analogous « carried by the assemblies only », row 2 lacks it.

The l.1341 half DUPLICATES the existing defi:causal_Ealpha paper finding (causal_Ealpha_lt_singLine, T-ett-e-models-bprime) and adds only the weaker causality hypothesis and the global form component_timelike (finding 1 above).

findings_review.claim: Finding 2 (a): the route of l.1529–1530 through prop:GX_sing_dec and « since M is a differential manifold, it is parametrisable by ℝ » is not needed. The X_A-charts into E_κ give a translation atlas, because two charts near the line differ by a time translation times a rotation (BTZ_1 prop:isom, local form).
findings_review.level: proof-level. DUPLICATE in substance of lem:past_BTZ PF1 (T-ett-line-development), which already says « the charts of E₀ and E_κ make the transitions along the line translations, and the development … needs only M Hausdorff and Δ closed ». What is new is only its α > 0 instance in Lean (BPrimeEAlpha.prop_isom_local inside SFAMassiveLine.isTranslationAtlas). findings_review.claim: Finding 2 (b): the time orientation is implicit. « Locally chronal » gives « a chronal curve » (l.1531–1533) only for a parametrisation that is future-directed in every chart; the translation transitions never reverse the chart time, so the chart time orients the whole component.
findings_review.level: proof-level, NEW: no curation row and no earlier audit mentions orientation at l.1531–1533 (grep). The gap is small: the orientation is also forced by every chart being a causal isomorphism, and a reversed parametrisation can simply be flipped. Better folded as one clause into the merged PF1 append than forwarded as a separate finding. At α = 0 the analogous point is a reading (OQ-35, « lightlike »), as T-ett-sfa-line-e0's REPORT records.

findings_review.claim: Finding 2 (c): Hausdorff (ETT.tex:255) is used (uniqueness of line arcs, LineDevelopment.exists_development).
findings_review.level: proof-level. DUPLICATE of PF1 (« needs only M Hausdorff ») and of the T-ett-line-development notes. massive_line carries [T2Space M]; sing_locallyChronal does not need it. « Used » is accurate; necessity is not claimed and is not shown.

findings_review.claim: Finding 2 (d): « parametrisable by ℝ » is a homeomorphism onto the component only when M is causal; a compact component is the image of a periodic γ; by hand, E_κ modulo rotShift T 0 has a circle as sing_κ.
findings_review.level: proof-level. True in substance, worded too strongly (finding 2 above). It DUPLICATES lem:past_BTZ PF0 and its findings_triage entry, which already name E_κ modulo a translation along the singular line. The by-hand example is sound: rotShift T 0 = (t, x) ↦ (t + T, x) is a chart isomorphism (chartIso_rotShift), and ℤ acts freely and properly discontinuously, so the quotient is a Hausdorff, second countable E_κ-manifold whose sing_κ is a circle and which is not causal.

question.asked: What is defi:causal_Ealpha's l.1341 (« For α>0 the singular line is timelike, hence locally chronal ») a statement of, the model E_α or M? The closer proposes OQ-87.
question.assessment: Not open, so no OQ-87. (1) As printed it is a statement of the model. « The singular line » is the notation of l.1332 (« We write sing(E_α) for the singular line »), inside a definition titled « Causal structure of the model spaces ». Its model form is singLine_lt / singLine_locallyChronal / singLine_chronalCurveOn, all in the row. (2) The paper uses it at M only « read in a chart », the pattern it names itself at l.1361 (rem:btz_pas_tarentin: « Definitions … read in a chart »), e.g. at l.1531 for a component Δ ⊆ M. The row already takes that reading, audited: EModelsBPrime.causal_Ealpha_lt_singLine, with the paper finding « confirmed at every E_{>=0}-manifold ». This target adds a variant (sing_locallyChronal) and a global form (component_timelike) under the same reading. (3) The causality at M is OQ-18, the group OQ-82, and E₀ in the family OQ-34/OQ-35, all open and all already in the row's blocked_on. No ruling on « model or M » would change a statement or a mark: the row stays partial and unmarked on those OQs in any case. (4) This is the precedent of T-ett-sfa-btz-e0's AUDIT-1, which judged the same question for defi:causal_E0 not open and recorded the reading as a note. Here the case is weaker still, since the M-level reading was already curated. Record it in defi:causal_Ealpha's notes.

lem:past_BTZ.notes_append: T-ett-sfa-massive-line (atlas-team, 2026-11-21), audit AUDIT-1 minor, Causal/Port/SFAMassiveLine.lean. (a) for α > 0 is the field massive_line, exactly, at every Hausdorff E≥0-manifold, mixed ones included, for every causality with an isomorphic chart at each point. It uses no absolute minimality, no second countability and no connectedness. Each component of sing_α(M) is the range of a γ : ℝ → M with γ 0 = p, inextensible, chronal over every segment, and a closed embedding when C is causal (massive_line; for the natural causality, massive_line_of_isAtlasCausalityDEC25). The proof is LineDevelopment.exists_chronal_line on the translation atlas of sing_κ(M), κ ≠ 2π, given by the X_A-charts into E_κ that are chart isomorphisms (isTranslationAtlas): τ is the time coordinate, σ r = e⁻¹(r, apex), and the transitions come from one BPrimeEAlpha.prop_isom_local each. The inverse charts are chronal along the line (chronalCurveOn_lineσ, the l.1531 use of defi:causal_Ealpha). The case α = 2π is vacuous (sing_{2π}(M) = ∅). A cover chart into E₀ at a massive point is excluded by cross-type invariance, so E₀ enters the hypothesis. Assemblies, at a T2, second countable E≥0-manifold with C absolutely minimal: SingularFlatAxioms ⇔ the field line (singularFlatAxioms_iff_line), and SingularFlatAxioms holds when sing₀(M) = ∅ (singularFlatAxioms_of_sing_zero; E_{>0}-manifolds, singularFlatAxioms_of_massive). Witness: E_π, the library's first SingularFlatAxioms instance with a non-empty massive line (epi_singularFlatAxioms; the line through (0, apex) is a closed embedding onto sing_π(E_π) = singLine π, nonvacuous_epi).
